en.headline: SFC to review IPO book-building process after fraud cases
en.dek: Chief executive Julia Leung said the regulator would work with the stock exchange to tighten procedures and urged professionals to report red flags.
body: The Securities and Futures Commission will review the book-building and filing process for initial public offerings in Hong Kong after a series of alleged fraud cases, its chief executive said on Monday. Julia Leung announced the move while speaking at a Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum.

Leung said the review follows last month’s enforcement action in which the SFC froze more than HK$4.6 billion in assets linked to three suspected IPO manipulation cases. On the day of the raids the regulator sent a circular to sponsors and underwriters reminding them to stay alert for undisclosed arrangements and to report any red flags.

She urged finance professionals to report under-the-table arrangements or other irregularities during the IPO process. Leung noted that about 30 per cent of current Hong Kong listings involve companies that have not yet turned a profit, and said the commission continues to strengthen the secondary market as well.

zh.headline: 證監會將檢討IPO簿記建檔流程以應對造假風險
zh.dek: 行政總裁梁鳳儀表示會與港交所合作收緊程序，並呼籲業界舉報可疑情況。
body: 證券及期貨事務監察委員會行政總裁梁鳳儀周一表示，證監會將檢討香港首次公開招股的簿記建檔及申報流程，以應對一連串涉嫌造假個案。她在彭博全球監管論壇上作出有關宣布。
梁鳳儀說，檢討是在上月執法行動後進行，證監會當時凍結超過46億港元資產，涉及三宗涉嫌IPO操縱個案。行動當日，監管機構向保薦人及包銷商發出通函，提醒他們對未披露安排保持高度警覺，並舉報任何可疑情況。
她呼籲金融專業人士在IPO過程中舉報任何「桃底安排」或其他異常情況。梁鳳儀指出，目前約三成香港上市個案涉及尚未錄得盈利的公司，證監會亦持續加強二級市場監管。
